name: rftools-mcp

tools.name: list_calculators
tools.description:
List the RF and electronics calculators on rftools.io, or those in one category.
Inputs: category, optional: one of rf, pcb, power, signal, antenna, general, motor, protocol, emc, thermal, sensor, unit-conversion, audio, iot. An unknown category is refused with this list.
Example: {"category":"pcb"}
Returns: A JSON array with each calculator's slug, title, category and description. search_calculators finds one by words instead of listing all 257.

category.description: Calculator category to filter by: rf, pcb, power, signal, antenna, general, motor, protocol, emc, thermal, sensor, unit-conversion, audio, iot

tools.name: search_calculators
tools.description:
Find the calculators that fit a task described in words, in English or in any of the languages rftools.io is published in.
Inputs: query, the words to match (required; English, de, es, fr, ja, ko, pt); category, optional: one of rf, pcb, power, signal, antenna, general, motor, protocol, emc, thermal, sensor, unit-conversion, audio, iot; limit, optional, 1 to 25 results (default 10).
Example: {"query":"trace impedance on FR4 microstrip","limit":5}
Returns: The matches, highest score first, each with slug, title, category, a one-line description, the page URL and its score, plus how many calculators matched in all. A search that matches nothing is reported as an error saying so, not as an empty list. Pass a slug to get_calculator_schema or run_calculation.

query.description: What to look for, in words (e.g. "trace impedance on FR4 microstrip")

category.description: Only calculators in this category: rf, pcb, power, signal, antenna, general, motor, protocol, emc, thermal, sensor, unit-conversion, audio, iot

limit.description: How many results to return, 1 to 25 (default 10)

tools.name: get_calculator_info
tools.description:
Describe one calculator: its inputs with units, defaults and bounds, its outputs, formula and keywords.
Inputs: slug, a calculator identifier from list_calculators or search_calculators.
Example: {"slug":"microstrip-impedance"}
Returns: The calculator's slug, title, category and description; its inputs (key, label, unit, defaultValue, min, max, tooltip); its outputs (key, label, unit, tooltip); the formula and keywords. get_calculator_schema returns the same inputs as a JSON Schema.

tools.name: get_calculator_schema
tools.description:
Give the exact input contract of one calculator as a JSON Schema, with its outputs, formula reference and page URL.
Inputs: slug, a calculator identifier. A misspelt one is refused, naming the closest identifiers.
Example: {"slug":"microstrip-impedance"}
Returns: inputSchema, a JSON Schema 2020-12 object whose properties are the input keys, each a number with its unit (x-unit), minimum, maximum, default and description; outputs (key, label, unit); formula (primary text, LaTeX where there is one, and the reference it comes from); and url.

tools.name: run_calculation
tools.description:
Compute a calculator's outputs for given inputs, locally in this server, with no API key.
Inputs: slug, and inputs keyed by the calculator's input names in the units get_calculator_schema reports. An input left out takes its declared default and is listed in defaultedInputs; a key the calculator does not declare is not read and is named in a warning; a value outside the declared range is still computed, with a warning naming the range.
Example: {"slug":"microstrip-impedance","inputs":{"traceWidth":3,"substrateHeight":1.6,"dielectricConstant":4.3}}
Returns: slug; results, one per output with key, label, value and unit; webUrl; defaultedInputs; warnings and errors when there are any; and provenance: the formula source, assumptions, whether the inputs lie in the range the calculator is stated for, the inputs used and the engine version.

inputs.description: Input values keyed by input name (e.g. {"traceWidth": 1.2, "substrateHeight": 1.6})

tools.name: solve_calculation
tools.description:
Find the value of one calculator input that makes an output equal a target, such as the trace width that gives 50 Ω on microstrip-impedance.
Inputs: slug; inputs, the calculator's other inputs keyed by name in its units; solveFor, the input to solve; target {output, value}; grid, optional, a step to round the answer to; range [low, high], required when solveFor states no bound. get_calculator_schema states every input and output key, unit and bound.
Example: {"slug":"microstrip-impedance","inputs":{"substrateHeight":1.6,"dielectricConstant":4.2,"copperThickness":35},"solveFor":"traceWidth","target":{"output":"impedance","value":50}}
Returns: The solved value (rounded to the grid when one is given, with the unrounded value), reached, which is false when no value in the range meets the target and the nearest value found is returned instead, the number of evaluations, warnings, and the full calculator result at that value with its provenance.
Runs on rftools.io, not locally: it needs RFTOOLS_API_KEY and spends one metered call from the account's monthly allowance, like POST /calculate.

inputs.description: The calculator's other inputs, keyed by input name (the input named by solveFor is not one of these — e.g. {"substrateHeight": 1.6, "dielectricConstant": 4.2, "copperThickness": 35})

solveFor.description: Which declared numeric input to solve for (e.g. "traceWidth")

output.description: The output key to bring to a value (e.g. "impedance")

value.description: The value that output should equal

grid.description: Round the solved value to the nearest multiple of this manufacturing grid, e.g. 0.001 (mm). Omit for the unrounded solution.

range.description: [low, high], narrowing the search inside solveFor's stated bound. Required when get_calculator_schema shows no minimum or maximum for solveFor.

tools.name: simulate_antenna_sim
tools.description:
Solve your own wire antenna with the NEC-2 method of moments: dipoles, Yagis, verticals and loops, element by element.
Inputs: Units, ranges and defaults are in each parameter's schema; one left out takes its default. Free lane: solveMode cannot be optimize without a paid key. Cross-parameter checks: sweep_stop_after_start. Time budget 1200 s; waitSeconds (default 90, max 600) bounds the wait.
Example: {"solveMode":"instant","freq":146000000}
Returns: Peak gain, front-to-back (one direction behind) and front-to-rear (worst of the rear half) ratios, beamwidths, feed impedance and VSWR (per frequency on a sweep, with the VSWR bandwidth), the azimuth and elevation patterns described as series, and for Optimize the recommended design and its Pareto front. Also warnings, provenance and the result page link; series are described, not listed (full: true returns everything). If waitSeconds runs out first: the jobId and progress, and the job keeps running.
Runs as a job on rftools.io and counts against the monthly run allowance (free lane without a key).

solveMode.description: Solve Mode. Instant is a closed-form textbook model of a preset. Standard solves your geometry with NEC-2 at one frequency; Sweep solves it across a band; Optimize searches element lengths and spacings. omit for the default of "instant". Paid tier only: optimize.

freq.description: Frequency (Hz). min 1000. omit for the default of 146000000

referenceImpedance.description: Reference Impedance (Ω). Impedance the reported VSWR and reflection coefficient are referred to. min 0.1. omit for the default of 50. Advanced — most callers can leave it out

wires.description: Wire Geometry. Wire segments of the antenna. Required for every mode but Instant. Array of {start:[x,y,z] in metres, end:[x,y,z] in metres, radius in metres, segments}. Each segment must be no longer than λ/10 and no shorter than 8 wire radii. Not on the web form, which has an editor for it — give it here as described

feed.description: Feed Point. Which wire and segment the source drives. Required for every mode but Instant. Object {wire, segment}, both 0-based: which wire the source drives, and which segment of it. Not on the web form, which has an editor for it — give it here as described

ground.description: Ground. Object {type: free_space | perfect | finite}, plus epsilonR and conductivity (S/m) when finite. Omit for free space. Advanced — most callers can leave it out

conductor.description: Conductor. Object {material: copper | aluminium | perfect | custom}, plus conductivity (S/m) when custom. Omit for copper. Advanced — most callers can leave it out

optimize.description: Search Settings. Object for the NSGA-II search (pymoo): {populationSize 8-200, generations 1-200, lengthRange, spacingRange, maxBoomLength (m), goals, leadGoal, buildTolerance {mm 0.1-50, trials 10-200}, heightRange [low, high] (m)}. goals: [{figure: peakGain | frontToBack (180°) | frontToRear (worst lobe 90-270° behind the beam) | vswr | elevationGain, role: optimize | threshold | off, min (gains and ratios) or max (vswr) for a threshold, reading: worst | average (vswr), elevationDeg}], at most 3 optimised; elevationGain and heightRange need a ground. Omit goals for gain, F/B and VSWR with the 2:1 rule. Give freqStart/freqStop/freqPoints to read every goal across a band. Applies when solveMode is "optimize". Advanced — most callers can leave it out

freqStart.description: Sweep Start (Hz). Lower bound of the band. Required in Sweep mode over frequency; in Optimize, gives the band every goal is read across. min 1000. Applies when solveMode is "sweep". Not on the web form, which has an editor for it — give it here as described

freqStop.description: Sweep Stop (Hz). Upper bound of the band. Required in Sweep mode over frequency; in Optimize, gives the band every goal is read across. min 1000. Applies when solveMode is "sweep". Not on the web form, which has an editor for it — give it here as described

freqPoints.description: Sweep Points. How many frequencies the band has. Each costs one solve per design in Optimize. min 2, max 2001. omit for the default of 51. Applies when solveMode is "sweep". Advanced — most callers can leave it out

sweepVariable.description: Sweep Variable. What the sweep varies: frequency across the band, or the mounting height (the feed's height above the ground) at one frequency, over perfect or real ground. omit for the default of "frequency". Applies when solveMode is "sweep". Advanced — most callers can leave it out

heightStart.description: Lowest Height (m). The lowest mounting height of a height sweep, in metres: the feed segment's centre above the ground. The whole antenna must stay above the ground. min 0. Applies when sweepVariable is "height". Advanced — most callers can leave it out

heightStop.description: Highest Height (m). The highest mounting height of a height sweep, in metres. min 0. Applies when sweepVariable is "height". Advanced — most callers can leave it out

heightPoints.description: Height Points. How many heights the sweep solves, evenly spaced; each is one solve. min 2, max 201. omit for the default of 21. Applies when sweepVariable is "height". Advanced — most callers can leave it out

antennaType.description: Closed-Form Model. Which textbook model Instant evaluates. Instant has no model for other geometries. omit for the default of "dipole". Applies when solveMode is "instant". Advanced — most callers can leave it out

groundType.description: Closed-Form Ground. Ground the closed-form model assumes. Instant only. omit for the default of "free_space". Applies when solveMode is "instant". Advanced — most callers can leave it out

randomSeed.description: Random Seed. Blank derives the seed from the parameters, so the same job repeats exactly. Set it to draw a different sample of the same design. min 0. Advanced — most callers can leave it out

waitSeconds.description: How long to wait for the result before returning the job id (0 = submit and return at once, max 600).

full.description: Return the whole result payload instead of the summary. Large.

tools.name: simulate_emi_radiated
tools.description:
Estimate radiated emissions from PCB loops and cables using Paul's analytical DM/CM models.
Inputs: Units, ranges and defaults are in each parameter's schema; one left out takes its default. Time budget 240 s; waitSeconds (default 90, max 600) bounds the wait.
Example: {"standard":"fcc_b","measDist":3,"dmCurrent_mA":5,"loopArea_cm2":0.5,"cmCurrent_uA":2,"cableLen_m":1,"fClk_MHz":480,"dutyCycle":50,"tRise_ns":0.5,"nTrials":100000} (the "USB 2.0 Trace Loop" preset)
Returns: Pass or fail against the chosen limit, the margin at the 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles, the strongest harmonics, and the emission spectrum and limit line described as series. Also warnings, provenance and the result page link; series are described, not listed (full: true returns everything). If waitSeconds runs out first: the jobId and progress, and the job keeps running.
Runs as a job on rftools.io and counts against the monthly run allowance (free lane without a key).

standard.description: Regulatory Standard. omit for the default of "fcc_b"

measDist.description: Measurement Distance (m). FCC Class B: 3 m. FCC Class A / CISPR: 10 m. Limits scale automatically. min 1, max 30. omit for the default of 3

dmCurrent_mA.description: DM Loop Current (peak) (mA). Peak current circulating in the PCB loop (e.g., power rail decoupling current). min 0.001, max 1000. omit for the default of 10

loopArea_cm2.description: Loop Area (cm²). Area of the current loop on the PCB. Smaller = less DM radiation. min 0.001, max 1000. omit for the default of 1

cmCurrent_uA.description: CM Cable Current (peak) (µA). Common-mode current on attached cables. Even µA levels can dominate emissions. min 0.001, max 10000. omit for the default of 1

cableLen_m.description: Cable Length (m). Length of the longest unshielded cable attached to the PCB. min 0.01, max 10. omit for the default of 0.5

fClk_MHz.description: Clock Frequency (MHz). Fundamental clock frequency. Harmonics are computed up to 1 GHz. min 1, max 2000. omit for the default of 100

dutyCycle.description: Duty Cycle (%). 50% duty cycle suppresses even harmonics. Other values can excite them. min 1, max 99. omit for the default of 50

tRise_ns.description: Rise Time (ns). Signal 10%–90% rise time. Longer rise times reduce high-frequency harmonics. min 0.1, max 100. omit for the default of 1

nTrials.description: Monte Carlo Trials. More trials = tighter confidence intervals. 100K is a good balance. min 1000, max 500000. omit for the default of 100000

randomSeed.description: Random Seed. Blank derives the seed from the parameters, so the same job repeats exactly. Set it to draw a different sample of the same design. min 0. Advanced — most callers can leave it out

waitSeconds.description: How long to wait for the result before returning the job id (0 = submit and return at once, max 600).

full.description: Return the whole result payload instead of the summary. Large.

tools.name: simulate_eye_diagram
tools.description:
Upload a Touchstone (.s2p) file and generate a PRBS eye diagram.
Inputs: Units, ranges and defaults are in each parameter's schema; one left out takes its default. Takes 1 to 1 .s2p/.s4p file(s) via inputFiles (inline) or inputPaths (local paths); the server uploads them. Uploading a file needs an API key; set RFTOOLS_API_KEY. Time budget 120 s; waitSeconds (default 90, max 600) bounds the wait.
Example: {"dataRate":10000000000,"prbs":"prbs15","samplesPerUI":64,"launchSwing":2000,"equalization":"none","maskType":"none","inputPaths":["/path/to/file.s2p"]}
Returns: Eye height (also as a share of the swing), width and jitter at the best or a stated sampling phase, any mask's pass and margin, any CTLE's gain, peaking and the eye before it, the file's details and loss at Nyquist, and the eye traces, impulse response and transfer function as series. Also warnings, provenance and the result page link; series are described, not listed (full: true returns everything). If waitSeconds runs out first: the jobId and progress, and the job keeps running.
Runs as a job on rftools.io and counts against the monthly run allowance (free lane without a key).

dataRate.description: Data Rate (bps). e.g. 10e9 for 10 Gbps. min 1000000. omit for the default of 10000000000

prbs.description: PRBS Length. omit for the default of "prbs15"

samplesPerUI.description: Samples per UI. min 16, max 128. omit for the default of 64

launchSwing.description: Launch Swing (mV). Peak-to-peak amplitude at the transmitter. Eye heights and the mask margin scale with it; 2000 mV (±1 V) is what the tool assumed before it could be set. min 10, max 5000. omit for the default of 2000

equalization.description: Receiver Equalization. CTLE applies the IEEE 802.3 Annex 93A reference continuous-time linear equalizer to the channel before the eye is built. omit for the default of "none"

ctleDcGain.description: CTLE DC Gain (dB). Zero at a quarter of the baud rate, poles at a quarter and at the baud rate. Blank tries -12 to 0 dB in 1 dB steps and keeps the gain with the largest eye height. min -12, max 0. Applies when equalization is "ctle".

maskType.description: Eye Mask. A mask centred on the sampling point and on 0 V, checked against every simulated bit. omit for the default of "none"

maskHalfHeight.description: Mask Half-Height (mV). The mask spans ± this voltage about 0 V. min 1, max 2500. omit for the default of 70. Applies when maskType is "hexagon" or "rectangle".

maskWidth.description: Mask Width (UI). A hexagon keeps its full height over the middle half of this width and tapers to a point at each end. min 0.05, max 1. omit for the default of 0.5. Applies when maskType is "hexagon" or "rectangle".

samplingPhase.description: Sampling Phase (UI). Where the receiver samples, measured from the mean zero crossing: 0.5 is the middle of the unit interval. Blank uses the point with the largest eye height and reports its phase. min 0, max 1

lossFrequency.description: Report Loss At (Hz). Also report the channel insertion loss at this frequency, e.g. 10e9. The loss at Nyquist is always reported. min 1000, max 1000000000000

inputFiles.description: 1–1 file(s), .s2p, .s4p. Uploading a file needs an API key; set RFTOOLS_API_KEY. Inline content; at most 5 MB in one call. The server uploads them and passes the keys.

name.description: File name including its extension, e.g. "channel.s4p"

inputPaths.description: 1–1 file(s), .s2p, .s4p. Uploading a file needs an API key; set RFTOOLS_API_KEY. Paths on this machine, read by the server and uploaded.

waitSeconds.description: How long to wait for the result before returning the job id (0 = submit and return at once, max 600).

full.description: Return the whole result payload instead of the summary. Large.

tools.name: simulate_fdtd_sparam
tools.description:
Solve microstrip stubs, coupled-line filters, via transitions, and step discontinuities across a ladder of named solve modes — from a 2D cross-section in seconds to a fine 3D openEMS field solve.
Inputs: Units, ranges and defaults are in each parameter's schema; one left out takes its default. Free lane: solveMode cannot be normal or fine without a paid key. Cross-parameter checks: sweep_span_within_center. Time budget 32400 s; waitSeconds (default 90, max 600) bounds the wait.
Example: {"structureType":"microstrip_open_stub","substrateName":"FR4","subEr":4.4,"subH":1.6,"subTanD":0.02,"traceW":3}
Returns: The solve mode and method actually used, S11 and S21 in dB and the Smith-chart traces described as series, the summary figures such as resonance, notch depth and input impedance, and flags for a degraded or physically invalid result. Also warnings, provenance and the result page link; series are described, not listed (full: true returns everything). If waitSeconds runs out first: the jobId and progress, and the job keeps running.
Runs as a job on rftools.io and counts against the monthly run allowance (free lane without a key).

structureType.description: Structure. omit for the default of "microstrip_open_stub"

substrateName.description: Substrate. omit for the default of "FR4"

subEr.description: Dielectric Constant. min 1, max 20. omit for the default of 4.4. Applies when substrateName is "custom".

subH.description: Substrate Height (mm). min 0.1, max 10. omit for the default of 1.6. Applies when substrateName is "custom".

subTanD.description: Loss Tangent. min 0, max 0.1. omit for the default of 0.02. Applies when substrateName is "custom".

traceW.description: Trace Width (mm). min 0.1, max 20. omit for the default of 3

traceL.description: Trace Length (mm). min 1, max 200. omit for the default of 30

stubL.description: Stub Length (mm). min 1, max 100. omit for the default of 15. Applies when structureType is "microstrip_open_stub".

gapW.description: Coupling Gap (mm). min 0.05, max 5. omit for the default of 0.2. Applies when structureType is "coupled_line_filter".

viaDia.description: Via Diameter (mm). min 0.1, max 2. omit for the default of 0.3. Applies when structureType is "through_via".

viaAR.description: Via Aspect Ratio. min 1, max 20. omit for the default of 5. Applies when structureType is "through_via".

w2.description: Output Trace Width (mm). min 0.1, max 20. omit for the default of 1.5. Applies when structureType is "step_discontinuity".

freqCenter.description: Center Frequency (Hz). min 100000000. omit for the default of 2400000000

freqSpan.description: Frequency Span (Hz). min 100000000. omit for the default of 4000000000

solveMode.description: Solve Mode. Instant solves a 2D cross-section and cascades published models — seconds, engineering accuracy. Express and above run a real 3D FDTD field solve on progressively finer meshes. omit for the default of "instant". Paid tier only: normal, fine.

copperT.description: Copper Thickness (mm). 0.035 mm is 1 oz copper. min 0.005, max 0.5. omit for the default of 0.035. Advanced — most callers can leave it out

roughness.description: Surface Roughness (µm). RMS copper roughness used by the Hammerstad/Huray correction. min 0, max 10. omit for the default of 0.6. Advanced — most callers can leave it out

waitSeconds.description: How long to wait for the result before returning the job id (0 = submit and return at once, max 600).

tools.name: simulate_filter_monte_carlo
tools.description:
Analyse how component tolerances affect your filter's passband ripple and stopband rejection.
Inputs: Units, ranges and defaults are in each parameter's schema; one left out takes its default. Free lane: monteCarloIterations max 1000. Cross-parameter checks: filter_parts_ladder, filter_pass_criteria. Time budget 180 s; waitSeconds (default 90, max 600) bounds the wait.
Example: {"filterType":"butterworth","bandType":"lowpass","order":5,"freqCutoff":1000000000,"ripple":0.5,"impedance":50}
Returns: The yield and its 95% confidence interval against the ripple and rejection limits or the entered pass criteria and a target, failures and statistics per criterion with each part's share of the variance, failing trials, what-ifs on the same trials, and the envelope, sample trials and responses as series. Also warnings, provenance and the result page link; series are described, not listed (full: true returns everything). If waitSeconds runs out first: the jobId and progress, and the job keeps running.
Runs as a job on rftools.io and counts against the monthly run allowance (free lane without a key).

filterType.description: Filter Type. omit for the default of "butterworth"

bandType.description: Band Type. omit for the default of "lowpass"

order.description: Filter Order. min 2, max 9. omit for the default of 5

freqCutoff.description: Cutoff Frequency (Hz). -3 dB frequency for Butterworth; passband edge for Chebyshev. min 1000. omit for the default of 1000000000

ripple.description: Passband Ripple (dB). Chebyshev only. min 0.01, max 3. omit for the default of 0.5

impedance.description: System Impedance (Ω). min 1. omit for the default of 50

componentTolerance.description: Component Tolerance (%). min 0, max 50. omit for the default of 5

toleranceDistribution.description: Distribution. omit for the default of "uniform"

rippleSpec_db.description: Passband Variation Limit (optional) (dB). Largest peak-to-peak |S21| variation across the passband for a build to pass. Leave blank to allow 0.5 dB more than the standard-value design achieves. min 0, max 20

rejectionSpec_db.description: Stopband Rejection Minimum (optional) (dB). Smallest rejection a build must reach from 2× the cutoff upward (low-pass) or below half the cutoff (high-pass). Leave blank to allow 3 dB less than the standard-value design achieves. min 0, max 200

monteCarloIterations.description: Monte Carlo Trials. Free tier: max 1,000. Pro and API: up to 100,000, as many as fit the run time allowed for the ladder and criteria. min 50, max 100000. omit for the default of 500. bound on the free tier: max 1000

randomSeed.description: Random Seed. Blank derives the seed from the parameters, so the same job repeats exactly. Set it to draw a different sample of the same design. min 0. Advanced — most callers can leave it out

parts.description: Circuit Parts. The ladder as built, source to load, 1 to 20 parts: { ref, kind: L | C, position: series | shunt, value in henries or farads, tolerance in % (optional; Component Tolerance when absent) }. Simulated as given, with no E24 rounding. Blank synthesises the ladder from the filter type, band, order and cutoff. Advanced — most callers can leave it out

passCriteria.description: Pass Criteria. What a build must meet to pass, 1 to 8 criteria, in place of the passband variation and stopband rejection limits: { kind: insertionLoss, fStart, fStop, maxDb }, { kind: cutoff3dB, fMin, fMax } or { kind: attenuation, freq (or fStart and fStop), minDb }; frequencies in Hz. Advanced — most callers can leave it out

yieldTarget.description: Yield Target (optional) (%). The share of builds that must pass. Blank means 95 %. min 0, max 100. Advanced — most callers can leave it out

waitSeconds.description: How long to wait for the result before returning the job id (0 = submit and return at once, max 600).

full.description: Return the whole result payload instead of the summary. Large.

tools.name: simulate_impedance_field_solver
tools.description:
Solve a PCB cross-section with a 2-D field solver: microstrip, stripline, coplanar waveguide and differential pairs, with trapezoidal traces, plating, solder mask and mixed dielectrics.
Inputs: Units, ranges and defaults are in each parameter's schema; one left out takes its default. Free lane: solveMode cannot be yield or stackup without a paid key. Time budget 300 s; waitSeconds (default 90, max 600) bounds the wait.
Example: {"solveMode":"solve","planes":"bottom","layers":[{"thickness":0.0002,"er":4.3,"tanD":0.02}],"conductors":[{"role":"signal","boundary":1,"x":-0.000175,"width":0.00035,"thickness":0.000035}],"frequencies":[1000000000,5000000000]} (the "50 Ω surface microstrip, FR-4, 1 oz" preset)
Returns: Per frequency, Z0 or a pair's whole mode set with effective permittivity, delay, L and C, loss with validity flags, the stated uncertainty and any width or spacing solved for; a yield adds the pass fraction with its 95 % interval, histograms with the limits, the extreme samples and the tolerance to tighten first. Also warnings, provenance and the result page link; series are described, not listed (full: true returns everything). If waitSeconds runs out first: the jobId and progress, and the job keeps running.
Runs as a job on rftools.io and counts against the monthly run allowance (free lane without a key).

solveMode.description: Solve Mode. Solve: one cross-section, with loss at each frequency and, on request, the width for a target and the tolerance spread. Yield (Pro and API): draws whole boards within the tolerances and reports the fraction that meet the specification. Stack-up (Pro and API): searches a catalogue for stack-ups that meet every net class's impedance within the fabrication rules, ranked by loss. omit for the default of "solve". Paid tier only: yield, stackup.

structureFamily.description: Structure. The template the cross-section was built from, for labelling only; blank lets the solver name it. Advanced — most callers can leave it out

planes.description: Reference Planes. Bottom: one plane under the stack (microstrip). Both: planes below and above it (stripline). None: no plane, for coplanar waveguide with its own grounds. omit for the default of "bottom"

layers.description: Dielectric Layers. Required for any board: the stack from the bottom up, { thickness (m), er, tanD, dispersion: djordjevic-sarkar | none, refFreq (Hz) }. εr and tanδ are the values at refFreq (default 1 GHz). Empty puts the traces in air. Not on the web form, which has an editor for it — give it here as described

conductors.description: Conductors. Required for a solve or a yield (a stack-up search builds its own): one or two signal traces and any coplanar grounds, { role: signal | ground, boundary (layer boundary it sits on, 0 = bottom), x (left edge, m), width (bottom, m), thickness (m), topWidth or etchFactor, plating (m) }. Not on the web form, which has an editor for it — give it here as described

mask.description: Solder Mask. Conformal solder mask on the outer layer, both outer layers in a stack-up search: { er, tanD, dispersion, refFreq (Hz: where er and tanD were measured, default 1e9; 1e5 to 1e11 in a stack-up search), overTrace, overSubstrate, betweenTraces (m) }. Blank: no mask. Advanced — most callers can leave it out

copper.description: Copper. Copper conductivity (S/m, default 5.8e7) and roughness: { model: hammerstad-jensen, rms (m) } or { model: huray, noduleRadius (m), surfaceRatio }. Advanced — most callers can leave it out

frequencies.description: Frequencies. Frequencies in Hz at which impedance and loss are reported. Blank: 1 GHz. Advanced — most callers can leave it out

externalRamp.description: External Ramp (Se/Sn). Slope compensation as a fraction of the sensed inductor up-slope; 0 applies none. Above 50 % duty cycle the inductor-current loop needs m_c·D′ > 0.5, where m_c = 1 + Se/Sn. min 0, max 10. omit for the default of 0. Applies when controlMode is "peak_current".

compensatorType.description: Compensator. omit for the default of "type3"

compK.description: Compensator Gain (K) (rad/s). min 0.001. omit for the default of 2000. Applies when compensatorType is "type1", "type2" or "type3".

compFz1.description: Zero 1 Frequency (Hz). min 1. omit for the default of 500. Applies when compensatorType is "type1", "type2" or "type3".

compFz2.description: Zero 2 Frequency (Hz). min 1. omit for the default of 1500. Applies when compensatorType is "type3".

compFp1.description: Pole 1 Frequency (Hz). min 1. omit for the default of 20000. Applies when compensatorType is "type1", "type2" or "type3".

compFp2.description: Pole 2 Frequency (Hz). min 1. omit for the default of 50000. Applies when compensatorType is "type3".

compRc.description: Compensation Resistor (R_c) (Ω). R_c with C_c sets the compensator zero, 1/(2π·R_c·C_c), and with g_m and the divider the mid-band gain. min 1, max 10000000. omit for the default of 5760. Applies when compensatorType is "type2_ota".

compCc.description: Compensation Capacitor (C_c) (F). e.g. 8.2e-9 for 8.2 nF. min 1e-12, max 0.001. omit for the default of 8.2e-9. Applies when compensatorType is "type2_ota".

compChf.description: High-Frequency Capacitor (C_hf) (F). Sets the high-frequency pole, (C_c + C_hf)/(2π·R_c·C_c·C_hf). 0 leaves it out. min 0, max 0.000001. omit for the default of 1.1e-10. Applies when compensatorType is "type2_ota".

compGm.description: Amplifier Transconductance (g_m) (S). e.g. 1e-3 for 1 mS. min 0.000001, max 0.1. omit for the default of 0.001. Applies when compensatorType is "type2_ota".

compVref.description: Feedback Reference (V_ref) (V). The error amplifier’s reference. The feedback divider is V_ref/V_out, so V_ref may not exceed V_out. min 0.1, max 999. omit for the default of 0.8. Applies when compensatorType is "type2_ota".

solveFor.description: Solve For. Crossover places R_c, C_c and C_hf for the target crossover in peak-current mode: the zero at the load pole, the high-frequency pole at the lower of Fsw/2 and the ESR zero, each part snapped to its standard series. omit for the default of "none". Applies when compensatorType is "type2_ota".

targetCrossover.description: Target Crossover (Hz). Must be below Fsw/2. When left blank, a tenth of the switching frequency. min 1, max 5000000. Omit to let the service derive it: Fsw / 10. Applies when solveFor is "crossover".

resistorSeries.description: Resistor Series. omit for the default of "E96". Applies when solveFor is "crossover".

capacitorSeries.description: Capacitor Series. omit for the default of "E12". Applies when solveFor is "crossover".

minPhaseMargin.description: Minimum Phase Margin (°). The verdict, the Monte Carlo yield and the crossover solve all require at least this phase margin. min 0, max 90. omit for the default of 45

minGainMargin.description: Minimum Gain Margin (dB). The verdict, the Monte Carlo yield and the crossover solve all require at least this gain margin. min 0, max 40. omit for the default of 10

monteCarloTrials.description: MC Trials. Each trial re-evaluates T(s) with randomized component values. min 1000, max 500000. omit for the default of 200000

tolLoad.description: Load Tolerance (%). min 0, max 100. omit for the default of 30

tools.name: simulate_sparam_pipeline
tools.description:
Upload up to 4 Touchstone files and get component values (L, C, R, Q, self-resonance) for a single component, plus insertion loss, return loss, group delay, TDR and passband ripple — all in one automated report.
Inputs: Units, ranges and defaults are in each parameter's schema; one left out takes its default. Takes 1 to 4 .s1p/.s2p/.s3p/.s4p file(s) via inputFiles (inline) or inputPaths (local paths); the server uploads them. Uploading a file needs an API key; set RFTOOLS_API_KEY. Cross-parameter checks: sweep_stop_after_start. Time budget 120 s; waitSeconds (default 90, max 600) bounds the wait.
Example: {"refImpedance":50,"freqStart":0,"freqStop":0,"inputPaths":["/path/to/file.s1p"]}
Returns: The port count, frequency range and detected two-port topology, each analysis stage it ran (network representations, passivity, and the extracted R, L or C with Q and self-resonance) with its values described as series, and any advisories. Also warnings, provenance and the result page link; series are described, not listed (full: true returns everything). If waitSeconds runs out first: the jobId and progress, and the job keeps running.
Runs as a job on rftools.io and counts against the monthly run allowance (free lane without a key).

tools.description:
List the server-side simulation job types with their tool names, parameters, file rules, free-lane bounds and time budgets.
Inputs: none.
Example: {}

tools.name: submit_simulation
tools.description:
Start a simulation job named by its job type and return at once with its id, without waiting for the result.
Inputs: jobType, one of the 14 job types list_simulation_tools names; params, that job type's parameters, validated here against its contract before anything is sent (each one's unit, range and default is in the matching simulate_* tool's schema); inputFiles or inputPaths for a job type that takes files. Example: {"jobType":"antenna_sim","params":{"solveMode":"instant","freq":146000000}}
Returns: jobId, jobType, status, queue position, the time budget, a suggested wait and the result page URL. An identical submission inside 60 s returns the same job.
